name: FFmpeg
summary: Current upstream ffmpeg CLI compiled as a generic, full-featured browser WebAssembly distribution.

upstream.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later / GPL-2.0-or-later depending on enabled components

profiles.label: Browser Full
profiles.output: Generic ffmpeg CLI; output is chosen by CLI arguments
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

profiles.label: Browser Full GPL
profiles.output: Generic ffmpeg CLI with GPL/libx264 features
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Download one FFmpeg profile ZIP, extract it under your app, and point the thin runtime wrapper at the matching core files.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/ffmpeg/browser-ffmpeg.js"></script>
<script type="module">
async function remuxMp4(file) {
  const ffmpeg = await WasmZooFFmpeg.loadHosted({
    coreJsUrl: "/vendor/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-core.js",
    wasmUrl: "/vendor/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-core.wasm"
  });

  try {
    const result = await ffmpeg.exec(
      ["-i", "/input.mp4", "-c", "copy", "/output.mp4"],
      {
        files: [{ name: "/input.mp4", data: file }],
        outputs: ["/output.mp4"],
        onLog: ({ stream, message }) => console.log(stream, message)
      }
    );
    return result.files[0].data;
  } finally {
    ffmpeg.dispose();
  }
}
</script>
notes: Both full profiles require SharedArrayBuffer and cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP).
browser-full and browser-full-gpl use the same wrapper API and filenames; choose the GPL build only when you need its extra GPL components such as libx264.
Input and output paths are Emscripten MEMFS paths for each command.

capabilityMatrix.note: WASM Zoo exposes the real fftools/ffmpeg command surface.
Arguments run against MEMFS paths in the browser.
Native breadth varies by configure options; Zoo keeps a broad software-only set.
Kept in the GPL profile only because it changes the binary license.
Browser builds require SharedArrayBuffer / cross-origin isolation.
Target-specific optimization rather than a native capability.
Intentionally excluded from the generic browser target.
Browser media capture belongs to Web APIs rather than libavdevice hardware backends.
Native hardware/platform backends do not map to this browser WASM target.

notes: Full means a broad software FFmpeg build for the browser target, not every capability of every native FFmpeg build.
Both full profiles require SharedArrayBuffer and COOP/COEP because the upstream FFmpeg CLI requires a working thread backend.
Native networking, libavdevice capture APIs and hardware acceleration backends are deliberately reported as unsupported rather than hidden.
Each built release records actual file sizes, SHA-256 hashes, enabled FFmpeg CONFIG entries, features.json and ffmpeg-config.mak.
